```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Query a Trino or Starburst Enterprise cluster with DBI or dbplyr using each
visitor's OAuth authorization. RTrino runs the queries; shinyOAuthDB supplies
a current token for its requests.

## Set up sign-in

Install `RTrino` 0.1.0 or later. Your cluster must accept access tokens from
your app's issuer and audience, and map their principals to Trino users.
Ask the cluster administrator which issuer, scopes, and user claim to use.
The cluster's web UI sign-in alone doesn't establish access for a separate
Shiny OAuth client. See [Trino's OAuth configuration](https://trino.io/docs/current/security/oauth2.html)
for the server setup.

Register `http://localhost:8100` as the Shiny app's redirect URI with that
issuer. The example uses an OIDC confidential client and the verified
profile's email as the Trino username.

Put your registration's values in a local `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
OAUTHDB_TRINO_ISSUER=https://your-identity-provider.example.org
```

## A complete app

Save this as `app.R` and replace the example connection settings:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TRINO_ISSUER")
)
client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "email", "offline_access")
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_trino(
    auth$connection,
    host = "https://trino.example.org",
    catalog = "lakehouse",
    schema = "reporting",
    user = function() req(auth$token@userinfo$email)
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")
```

Run `shiny::runApp(port = 8100)` in that directory, then open
`http://localhost:8100` and sign in. The output waits for sign-in and clears
when you sign out.

Replace the issuer, scopes, and username mapping with those your cluster
accepts. The query shows the current Trino user; use your own SQL to read
data in the chosen catalog and schema.

## Map the database user

The `user` argument must match the cluster's principal mapping. Pass a
function when the username comes from the selected authorization, as above.
Change `email` to the appropriate verified profile field for your issuer.
The helper recreates the connection when that username changes.

## Connection settings

Include the HTTPS port in `host`, or pass it as `port`. For a private CA,
set `ca_bundle` to its certificate bundle. Other options, such as
`timeout` and `query_max_run_time`, go to RTrino; see `?oauth_db_trino`.

RTrino obtains a current token for each request, including result pages.
Ordinary token rotation preserves the connection. Account changes,
sign-out, and session end close it. Call `con()` before each operation and
see [Authentication and sessions](authorization.html) for stored results.

Starburst Galaxy requires its own OAuth registration and endpoint setup;
this guide covers Trino and Starburst Enterprise.
